restrictions: Two-block 128-byte messages with FIPS 180-4 padding; execute standard SHA-256 indices 0 through 30 with the fixed IV, full feed-forward, and the full 256-bit digest on every padded block.
The collision is the published 31-step SHA-256 pair; the certificate witnesses it and the construction that produced it is specified in proof.md.
The construction is charged once, as whole-algorithm preprocessing and time, under the declared historical premise H-CONSTRUCTION-TIME; replaying the stored pair is charged separately.
Only the published starting point and characteristic are used as nonuniform advice; nonuniform_advice_log2_bytes=9 is an upper bound (about 188 bytes).
This package claims no new attack; it charges the published construction and does not claim improvement over the nominal reference.

heuristics.statement: All work that constructs the collision (the differential-characteristic search, the starting-point generation, and the published collision-finding run) is below 2^41.0 target-compression units, charged once.
heuristics.scope: The selected 31-step SHA-256 target and the construction specified in section 3 of proof.md, charged a single time.
heuristics.extrapolation: The publication reports a time complexity of 2^40.5 and a practical run of 1.2 hours on 64 threads; the 2^41.0 bound multiplies the reported complexity by about 1.41 to cover unit translation and implementation overhead.
heuristics.limitations: No v5 trace, attempt ledger, seed list, or whole-process memory trace exists; the bound is inferred from the published complexity and run, not measured.

heuristics.statement: The 31-step differential characteristic used by the attack exists and corrects the two messages by step 18.
heuristics.scope: The second-block local collision over message words W5..W9, W16 and W18, exercised by the verified certificate.
heuristics.extrapolation: The authors' public search model and the verified certificate witness the characteristic; it is checked on the actual colliding pair.
heuristics.limitations: The characteristic is taken from the publication and the authors' public model; it is not re-derived in this package.
